<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/ai/agent.zod.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **177** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9a274e6725822124948fb54a3b3cebccf1c84e44` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `1c2e51ffc1fad1c64166b6488bb896bcb0e50ea0`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-ai/evals/skills-tools-knowledge.json,packages/spec/src/ai/agent.zod.ts + content/docs/ai/agents.mdx
Security-touching: yes

First record on PR #38003 for card #37967 (the follow-up to N2 and N3 of record 7219261608 on PR #37939). Read: the card body and its three comments (triage 7220504340, claim 7220959162, dev report 7221579739); the PR title, body, its 4-file list and its comments (docs-drift 7221594747, head comment 7222267895, review claim 7222287329); the net diff against the merge base `dc45b1e6` (+23/-5); the 70 check-runs on the head (60 success, 10 skipped, none failed). Nothing was checked out, built, run or re-run; git objects were read in place, and the two eval-file blobs were compared key by key as JSON. `origin/main` has moved to `30a8047b` since the base; the object-level merge of the head into it is clean (tree `96d4a2c4`).

`Security-touching: yes`, conservatively, as on PR #37939. The words this PR changes teach schema refusal only. But the changed `knowledge` row of `agents.mdx` carries, unchanged, the sentence that declaring sources on an agent "scoped nothing" and that retrieval is restricted per source, and eval case 5's changed string carries the knowledge-source restriction (`aiExposed`, `where`). Both are `main`'s text and still true; nothing security-relevant is newly taught. The seat decides the label.

### ① Derived judgments

- `skills/objectstack-ai/evals/skills-tools-knowledge.json`: one line, case 5, key `expected_output`. Compared as parsed JSON against the base: 12 cases on both sides, `skill_name` equal, and the single differing key in the whole file is case 5's `expected_output`. The prompt, `files` and `assertions` of case 5 are identical. `hashCase` (`packages/qa/scenarios/src/skill-evals/cases.ts:125`) reads the prompt, `mustContain`, `mustNotContain`, `mustContainAny`, `shouldTrigger` and `files`; it does not read `expected_output`. The case hash does not move, case 5's recorded rounds stay keyed, and no eval round is owed. Right.
- `packages/spec/src/ai/agent.zod.ts`: one comment hunk, 2 lines for 4, inside a block comment. No schema, type, export or accept set changes. Right.
- `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx`: two table rows, one clause each. Docs prose. Right.
- `.changeset/37967-retired-agent-keys-unknown-key-prose.md`: new. Right, see ②.
- Overlap in the eval file. PR #37969 (case 6, the any-of form) is already in this branch's base: `dc45b1e6` is that commit, and its one-line hunk sits in case 6. Since the base, `main` took PR #37937, whose hunk in this file is near line 94 (case 10). This PR's hunk is line 47 (case 5). The three hunks are disjoint and the merge into `30a8047b` is clean.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/skills` patch: right; the eval file ships in the skill bundle. `@objectstack/spec` patch: right; the package's `files` list publishes `src/**/*.zod.ts`, so the comment is published bytes, and a comment is a patch. The docs page belongs to no package and needs no entry. `Check Changeset` is green on the head.

Clause-②: no. Correct on the PR body and in the changeset: no accept set moves. `Metadata-protocol: none` is correct.

The changeset, sentence by sentence against the tree:
- Title, "the retired agent keys are refused as unknown keys, not tombstones": true.
- "`agent.tools` and `agent.knowledge` were removed in protocol 17, and their tombstones left the shape at protocol 18": true (`agent.test.ts:102-103` and `:233`; `content/docs/ai/tools.mdx:205`).
- "the strict `AgentSchema` refuses each as an unknown key, and the refusal names https://objectstack.ai/docs/protocol-upgrade": true for both keys (`agent.test.ts:101-114` and `:232-242`).
- "Three texts still described the older behaviour and now say what happens today": true, the three hunks.
- Skills bullet, "case 5's `expected_output` no longer calls the two keys protocol-17 tombstones. The case's prompt and assertions are unchanged": true, see ①.
- Spec bullet, "The comment ... on the removed `AIKnowledgeSchema` no longer says `agent.knowledge` is tombstoned below it. No schema, type or export changes": true.
- "The `ai/agents` docs page says the same in its `tools` and `knowledge` rows: the key is not on the type, so there is no `never` member for `tsc` to refuse by name": true, and worded with care. It does not claim that `tsc` is silent; see N2.
- "Nothing to migrate": true.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev report 7221579739: `open_questions` empty; `security_findings` none.
- Dev narrowing, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` not measured locally and the spec test run narrowed to six files: answered by the head's check-runs, none failed.
- The claim's serial note names PR #37937 (case 10) and the card's names card #37928 (case 6). Both hunks are now on `main` or in the base, and both are disjoint from case 5; see ①.
- The `longTerm.store` comment, deliberately left alone: correct. On the head the comment at `agent.zod.ts:518-519` says `longTerm.store` "is tombstoned below", and `:549` is `store: retiredKey(LONG_TERM_STORE_RETIRED)`. That tombstone is live (removed in 17.7.0 under ADR-0049) and the comment is true. Editing it would have been wrong.
- The dev's sweep for other keys described as tombstones, spot-checked on the head across `content/docs`, `skills` and `packages/spec/src` (tests and changelogs aside). No remaining text calls `agent.tools` or `agent.knowledge` a tombstone or typed `never`. The three places N2 and N3 of record 7219261608 named are the three this PR fixes. `content/docs/ai/knowledge-rag.mdx` has no mention of either key, of a tombstone, or of `never` in that sense. The other "tombstone" hits in `agent.zod.ts` (`model.provider` at :35-87, `lifecycle` at :414, `longTerm.store` at :519-549) each sit on a live `retiredKey()`. `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md:458` reads "tombstone gone in 18", PR #37939's landed text. The rest of `agents.mdx` (the callout at :320-330, the sample comment at :375-376) states only the removal and is true.
- Docs-drift comment 7221594747 reports no anchor for `agent.zod.ts`: expected for a comment-only hunk; the page that documents these keys is in this diff.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. No query, id materialisation or join in the diff.

### ④ Design judgment

**`skills/objectstack-ai/evals/skills-tools-knowledge.json`**, case 5, against the spec on `main` and the skill it grades. The new clause, "were removed in protocol 17: the strict schema refuses each as an unknown key, naming https://objectstack.ai/docs/protocol-upgrade", is true for both keys by the two tests cited under ②, and the URL is `PROTOCOL_UPGRADE_GUIDE_URL` letter for letter. It now agrees with the skill's own paragraph (`skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md:454-458` on the head, landed by PR #37939), so the reference answer and the text a model is taught say the same thing. The rest of the string is `main`'s. Tried to break it: the machine assertions do not read `expected_output`, the hash does not read it, so nothing a runner computes can move; the only reader is a person or a judge comparing prose, and the prose is now correct.

**`packages/spec/src/ai/agent.zod.ts`**, the comment hunk, sentence by sentence against the file on the head:
- "It typed `agent.knowledge`, which no key below declares any more": true. `AgentSchema` (:341 on the head) declares no `knowledge`, and neither its `aliases` nor its `guidance` map names it.
- "the RAG path never read the agent record, so the whole block was a grounding claim nothing enforced": `main`'s sentence, unchanged, and consistent with `agent.test.ts:219-222`.
- "The key's tombstone aged out at protocol 18": true (`agent.test.ts:233`).
- "so the strict `AgentSchema` refuses it as an unknown key naming the upgrade guide": true (`agent.test.ts:232-242`).
- The hunk is inside a block comment; no code line moves. `TypeScript Type Check`, `Type Check · source gates` and `Test Core` are green on the head.

**`content/docs/ai/agents.mdx`**, the two rows (read at the dispatching seat's request; outside `hits`, named after the `+` in Scope):
- "the key is not on the type": true. `Agent` is `z.input` of a strict object whose shape has neither key (`agent.zod.ts:649`).
- "the strict schema refuses it as an unknown key, naming the upgrade guide": true for each row, and the link is the constant's URL.
- "Removed in protocol 17", each row's why-sentence and each replacement are `main`'s text, unchanged.
- The dropped "a value that reaches the runtime is rejected at parse" is not lost: the strict-schema clause says it.
- The dropped "typed `never`" is rightly dropped; no such member exists.
- The dropped "writing it fails `tsc`": see N2.

N1 (nit) — `packages/spec/src/ai/agent.zod.ts:104-105`, the last sentence of the docblock this PR corrects, is unchanged and no longer true: "The protocol-17 `agent-knowledge-topics-to-sources` conversion remains in the chain". No registry or entry module on the head carries that id. `packages/spec/src/conversions/entries/17/sharing-rule-access-level-full-to-edit.ts:17` records it as ABSORBED, folded before release into the removal of the whole block, and `retired-after.census.json` has no row for it. The card named only "tombstoned below", so the PR meets its acceptance. A comment, with no effect on any schema or type; not a prose face, so it is left for a follow-up and not fixed on this head.

N2 (nit) — the rows no longer mention `tsc` at all, and one true fact goes with the false one. Read from the types, not measured: `defineAgent` takes `z.input` of the strict `AgentSchema` (`agent.zod.ts:645`), a closed object type, so an inline `defineAgent({ ... tools: [...] })` literal still fails `tsc` through the excess-property check. What ended at 18 is the `never` member that refused the key by name with its prescription, and the guarantee for values that arrive through a variable, a spread, or JSON. The new rows state nothing false ("the key is not on the type" is exact, and the changeset words it exactly), and the parse refusal they teach holds on every path. The card's and the PR body's reader summaries overstate it by saying the refusal is at run time only; that prose is the seat's. An optional half-clause for a later docs edit: an inline literal is still a type error, as an excess property. No test pins this, so it is offered as a reading.

No must-fix, no should-fix.
